item.title: Looking back at local milestones in West Norfolk
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at local milestones in West Norfolk
This week’s look back at local history highlights several notable events from past Octobers. In 2013, actor Tim Bentinck, known for his role in The Archers, officially opened the Hunstanton Heritage Centre. That same year, the Purfleet Trust in King’s Lynn secured a £114,000 lottery grant to support food bank users, while a misspelling on road signs at the Hardwick Industrial Estate was finally corrected.
Moving to 2017, King’s Lynn marked the 25th anniversary of the railway line’s electrification with a civic reception at the town hall. Other notable moments included the West Norfolk and King's Lynn Beekeepers Association celebrating their centenary and the unveiling of a new plaque at Downham Town Hall to preserve the history of its foundation stone.

item.title: Employment tribunal rejects unfair dismissal claim from former King’s Lynn head teacher
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Employment tribunal rejects unfair dismissal claim from former King’s Lynn head teacher
An employment tribunal has dismissed a claim of unfair dismissal brought by Greg Hill, the former head teacher of Howard Junior School in Gaywood. Mr Hill, who served at the school from 2007 until his arrest in 2023, was dismissed by the Eastern Multi-Academy Trust in April 2024 following a conviction for harassment.
Judge KJ Palmer ruled there was no evidence to support Mr Hill’s claims of a conspiracy against him, describing his assertions as groundless. During the proceedings, the tribunal noted that Mr Hill failed to engage with the dismissal process and did not provide medical evidence to support his absence from the hearing. The judge also refused his request to reveal the identities of witnesses involved in the case.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/not-a-shred-of-evidence-to-support-stalker-head-greg-hill-9485079/

item.title: Kent man fined after being found over alcohol limit in North Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Kent man fined after being found over alcohol limit in North Lynn
A 23-year-old scaffolder from Kent has been fined after being found in charge of a vehicle while over the legal alcohol limit. Joshua Kurszewski, of Stangate Drive in Sittingbourne, was discovered by police on Crossbank Road in North Lynn on September 9 after a recovery worker raised concerns. A breath test revealed he was more than double the legal limit.
Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court, Kurszewski admitted the offence. He was issued ten penalty points on his licence and ordered to pay a total of £645 in fines, surcharges, and costs. The court heard there was no evidence that he had been driving the vehicle at the time.

The Wisbech-based charity Feed Fenland is calling for community support to maintain its meal service for vulnerable residents. The organisation provides hot evening meals six nights a week at The Olive Academy on Coalwharf Road, often serving up to 200 portions per night.
Operating without government or large-scale charity funding, the service relies entirely on donations and volunteers to cover costs, which average £80 per night. The charity is currently seeking more people to assist with cooking, serving, and general operations. Those interested in volunteering or providing financial support can contact the team via email at correspondence@feedfenland.com.

King’s Lynn Dragon Festival returns next month
The King’s Lynn Dragon Festival is set to return on Saturday, November 7, offering a variety of free family activities across the town. Cultural and heritage venues will host performances, trails, and medieval-themed entertainment between 10am and 3pm.
Events include a dragon hunt, archery, and live shows at the Minster, alongside craft sessions at the local library. Several venues are participating, including the Lynn Museum, St George’s Guildhall, and True’s Yard. Free cinema screenings are also available at the Majestic and Corn Exchange, though tickets for these must be booked in advance. Residents are encouraged to check with individual venues, as some activities have limited capacity.
